dataset.notice: SYNTHETIC DEMO DATA - generated from documented rules. Not measured battery data. Upload your own CSV for operator data.

soh.target: State of Health (fraction of rated usable capacity)

eol.target: Months until SOH crosses the EOL threshold (80%)

anomaly.model: IsolationForest (one-class, fitted on known-good packs only)
anomaly.method: one-class novelty detection on the healthy-pack manifold

baseline_note: Baseline = predict the training mean for every battery. skill_vs_baseline_pct is the MAE reduction versus that naive predictor. A model that cannot beat the baseline is not worth deploying.

honesty.headline: READ THIS BEFORE QUOTING ANY NUMBER ABOVE
honesty.why_soh_r2_is_so_high: In this synthetic dataset the target SOH is generated by a known deterministic degradation law applied to the same feature columns the model reads. The features therefore nearly DETERMINE the label, so a tree ensemble can recover the law almost exactly and R2 approaches 1.0. A high R2 here is a property of the data-generating process, NOT evidence of real-world battery prediction accuracy. On measured fleet data the same model would score far lower.
honesty.what_would_change_this: Retraining on measured data from a real BMS or telematics feed (upload a CSV via POST /api/data/upload) replaces the synthetic label law with actual observations. Only then do these metrics mean anything.

limitations: Metrics are measured against SYNTHETIC ground truth, not measured batteries.
They are NOT estimates of real-world accuracy.
The very high SOH R2 is an artifact of the label being a deterministic function of the features.
Real-world accuracy requires retraining on measured fleet data.
Feature importance is correlational; the simulated law is not a causal model.
The EOL horizon is a projection that assumes the observed duty cycle continues.
Tree ensembles cannot extrapolate: predictions saturate outside the training range.
Anomaly scores are signals for review, never confirmed faults.
Pathway, priority and circularity outputs are transparent RULES, not learned models.

robustness_under_bms_noise.note: Measured on a held-out 20% split. 'clean' = synthetic features with no measurement error. 'with_bms_noise' = same batteries after realistic BMS sensor error is injected. The gap is the cost of real-world sensor noise.

not_hardcoded_check.verdict: PASS - predictions respond to input changes and move in the physically expected direction
